text:
[RDSC.5.5.7] `identity_role` declares the slot's identity role
per [LFAC.1.7]: `IDENTITY_ROLE_KEY` (the slot is part of the
schema's identity key), `IDENTITY_ROLE_MUTABLE` (payload) or
`IDENTITY_ROLE_ENGINE` (the engine's `ts`, [LFAC.9.1]: outside the key
and outside the no-op comparison). On a `logical` schema the compiler
emits `KEY` or `MUTABLE` for every author slot (require-all,
[LFAC.1.7.4]) and `ENGINE` for `ts`; on a non-`logical` schema every
slot is `IDENTITY_ROLE_UNSPECIFIED`. The runtime reads a `logical`
schema's identity key from its `KEY` slots — it does not infer identity
from slot 0 or from a slot named `entity_id` — and compares its `KEY`
and `MUTABLE` slots for the no-op test ([LFAC.2.5.1]).

alloy.name: rdsc_5_5_7__engine_iff_logical_ts
alloy.note: A slot carries ENGINE exactly when it is the ts of a logical schema: never an author's marker, and a non-logical ts is UNSPECIFIED. The partition said a second way. Bounded: six slots, six schemas; fails if the partition's ENGINE line is dropped.

alloy.name: rdsc_5_5_7__marked_iff_logical
alloy.note: A slot carries KEY or MUTABLE exactly when it is an author slot of a logical schema. The partition said a second way. Bounded: six slots, six schemas.

alloy.name: rdsc_5_5_7__role
alloy.note: The four roles the clause and proto/slot.proto#IdentityRole name: KEY, MUTABLE, ENGINE, UNSPECIFIED.

alloy.name: rdsc_5_5_7__role_partition
alloy.note: The clause's partition: on a logical schema every author slot is KEY or MUTABLE and ts is ENGINE; on any other schema every slot is UNSPECIFIED.
